Statements: B ≤ E > S < H ≤ K = Z
Conclusions:
I. H ≤ Z
II. B > K
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

Read the chain U > A = K > G > N > M from N to K and from G to K. A mix of > and < (or ≥ and ≤) between two letters breaks the link.
I: N < K always holds in the chain, so it follows.
II: G ≥ K can fail (e.g. G = 2, K = 3 fits every statement), so it does not follow.
Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

question:
6 friends Eshan, Farah, Hema, Lata, Priya, Rahul sit in a straight row facing north. Rahul sits somewhere between Priya and Lata. Priya and Lata are not neighbours. Lata sits somewhere between Priya and Farah. Farah sits somewhere between Lata and Hema. Hema sits somewhere between Priya and Eshan. Hema and Priya are not neighbours. Priya sits immediately to the left of Rahul. Farah sits somewhere to the left of Eshan.
Who sits at the extreme left end?
explanation:
Start with the clues that fix a position (ends, 'immediately left of'), then place the rest.
• Rahul sits somewhere between Priya and Lata.
• Priya and Lata are not neighbours.
• Lata sits somewhere between Priya and Farah.
• Farah sits somewhere between Lata and Hema.
• Hema sits somewhere between Priya and Eshan.
• Hema and Priya are not neighbours.
• Priya sits immediately to the left of Rahul.
• Farah sits somewhere to the left of Eshan.
Only one order satisfies every clue, left to right: Priya, Rahul, Lata, Farah, Hema, Eshan.
Who sits at the extreme left end? Priya.

question: Find the missing number: 3, 7, 14, ?, 37, 53, 72
explanation:
Differences: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19; each grows by 3.
So the missing term is 24.
Full series: 3, 7, 14, 24, 37, 53, 72.
